# tes-scripts.R

```{r}
devtools::load_all()

# generate trends
trends <- make_trends_dist(n = 500, d = 2, seed = 32026)
plot(trends$x1, type = "l", col = 'red',
     xlab = "t", ylab = expression(mu[t]))
lines(trends$x2, col = "blue")

# add ARMA noise
sim <- add_noise(trends,
                 h             = 30,
                 lambda_target = 4,
                 scale         = 1,
                 order         = c(2, 1),
                 s             = 100,
                 n_start       = 30,
                 seed          = 31726)

# summary of added noise processes
sim$noise

# plot observed series with true trends overlaid
plot(sim$y1, type = "l", col = 'red',
     xlab = 't', ylab = expression(X[t]))
lines(sim$y2, col = "blue")
lines(sim$x1, col = "darkgrey", lwd = 2)
lines(sim$x2, col = "darkgrey", lwd = 2)

# local moving average decoupling (method = "boot", "mc", or "analytic")
out <- lomad(sim$y1, sim$y2, q = 10, h = 50, B = 100, 
             seed = 31726, method = "boot", ncores = parallel::detectCores() - 1,
             verbose = TRUE)
out$p_values
out$observed
out$expected

# plot
plot_lomad_fit(sim$y1, sim$y2, out)

# plot smoothed trends only
plot(out$ma1, type = "l", col = "red")
lines(out$ma2, type = "l", col = "blue")
lines(out$trend_hat, type = 'l', col = 'grey')

```

```{r}

library(zoo)
library(roll)

# moving average window length
q <- 10
# window width - 
h <- 50

# correlation threshhold
x_thresh <- 0.8

# smoothed series
ma1 <- out$ma1
ma2 <- out$ma2

# estimated trend
# if you had to only estimate one - trend_hat
trend <- out$trend_hat

# smoothed noise
noise1_sm <- ma1 - trend
noise2_sm <- ma2 - trend

# oracle SNR: use the same h and s as the add_noise call so that the
# local variances here match what make_noise targeted during calibration.
# previous code used q=10 (MA window) and h=50 (variance window) which
# both differ from the add_noise parameters h=30 and s=100, causing
# lambda to appear far below lambda_target.
h_noise <- 30   # matches h in add_noise call above
s_noise <- 100  # matches s in add_noise call above

# MA-smooth true trend and true noise with add_noise's window
trend_sm_true <- roll::roll_mean(sim$x1, width = h_noise, min_obs = h_noise)
noise1_true   <- sim$y1 - sim$x1
noise2_true   <- sim$y2 - sim$x2
e1_sm         <- roll::roll_mean(noise1_true, width = h_noise, min_obs = h_noise)
e2_sm         <- roll::roll_mean(noise2_true, width = h_noise, min_obs = h_noise)

# local variances using add_noise's variance window
lv_signal <- roll::roll_var(trend_sm_true, width = s_noise, center = TRUE, min_obs = s_noise)
lv_noise1 <- roll::roll_var(e1_sm,         width = s_noise, center = TRUE, min_obs = s_noise)
lv_noise2 <- roll::roll_var(e2_sm,         width = s_noise, center = TRUE, min_obs = s_noise)

lambda1 <- lv_signal / lv_noise1
lambda2 <- lv_signal / lv_noise2

#rho 
rho_t <- sqrt((lambda1 * lambda2) /
              ((1 + lambda1) * (1 + lambda2)))

# starting with neff = h = 50 - will change later
n_eff <- h
z_t <- sqrt(n_eff) * (x_thresh - rho_t)
p_t <- pnorm(z_t)

plot(rho_t, type = "l")
plot(lv_signal, type = "l")

#histogram of lambdas 
hist(lambda1, 
     main = "Lambda 1",
     breaks = 50) 

hist(lambda2, main = "lambda 2", 
     breaks = 50)
```
